newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt criticises U.S. veto of Jerusalem resolution.
newsitem.headline: Egypt criticises U.S. veto of Jerusalem resolution.

text.p: Egypt criticised the U.S. veto of a U.N. Security Council resolution demanding Israel cease work on a controversial housing project in Jerusalem, saying the Jewish state might see it as carte blanche for illegal measures.

Foreign Minister Amr Moussa, speaking in the Pakistani capital Islamabad on Saturday, said the veto also appeared to contradict U.S. criticism of the Jewish settlement Israel is building at Hor Moma or Jabal Abu Ghneim in Arab East Jerusalem.

"We are worried that Israel will interpret the United States using its veto...as a green light to persevere in measures which violate all laws and agreements," he said. The minister was quoted in Egyptian government newspapers.
"We had expected that what the United States says would be translated into real positions and would not be just talk which is contradicted by a step such as the veto," he added.
The Security Council resolution, vetoed on Friday, called on Israel to halt work on new Jewish housing in East Jerusalem.
The vote on the draft, sponsored by Arab states, was 13 in favour, with the United States casting the only negative vote and Costa Rica abstaining.
Moussa also said that Jerusalem was under grave threat and that increasing frustration would lead to an explosion.
